title: John Lennon and Paul McCartney meet in New York City | 1971
content:
Paul and Linda McCartney paid a visit to John Lennon and Yoko Ono in New York City on 17 December 1971.

The McCartneys were in America with Wings for rehearsals, and had agreed to meet Lennon and Ono at 105 Bank Street in Manhattan. Lennon and McCartney had various legal issues to discuss, following the resolution of McCartney’s court case to dissolve The Beatles’ partnership.

The meeting was warm and cordial, with Lennon giving McCartney a copy of the Beatles bootleg Yellow Matter Custard. It contained BBC radio session recordings, but Lennon mistakenly believed the songs were from the group’s 1962 Decca audition.

The two men also discussed Lennon’s immigration issues in America, and his and Ono’s attempt to track down her estranged daughter Kyoko.

Lennon and McCartney agreed to end their private disagreements, and to put a stop to their very public exchange of words against one another. Lennon also finally agreed to McCartney’s request to end The Beatles’ partnership, although it would be some years before that took place.
